open.speaker: editor
lines: November 16th, 1966. Two couples, the TNT area, 'a large white creature' with red eyes that chased their car.
We ran it on the front page. I've regretted the headline every day since. Not the story. The headline.

passives.line: The 16th was a Wednesday. The sighting was the night of the 15th. He set that page in a few hours, on a weekly that usually took a week.
'Every day since.' He has counted them. Men who count the days are waiting for someone to tell them they can stop.
He said 'the headline' twice and is waiting for you to ask about it. A newspaperman always leaves the real story one question down.

options.text: You went to press the same night. Who typed it?
You regret it. So print a correction. This week.
(Let him look at the page a while.)

headline.speaker: editor
lines: 'COUPLES SEE MAN-SIZED BIRD... CREATURE... SOMETHING.' Three nouns and two sets of dots. I was tired and I was scared and I let the dots do the work.
A wire desk in Ohio turned 'something' into a name the next week. After that it was a cartoon, and the four of them were a punchline.
Dots are a confession. Every editor knows that.

typed.speaker: editor
lines: I did. Two fingers, one in the morning, with the four of them in that chair you're sitting in.
The girls weren't hysterical. The deputy wrote hysterical. I never printed it and I never printed that I didn't.
Two witnesses calm at one a.m. is better evidence than two witnesses screaming at eleven.

typed_fail.speaker: editor
lines: You weren't born. Don't tell me how my paper went out.
The deputy took the statement. I took the quote. You want the statement, go two doors down and ask him what he wrote and what he was told to write.

correction.speaker: editor
lines: I'd print one tomorrow if I had something true to correct it with. Twenty-eight years and nobody's brought me a fact. They bring me feelings.
Bring me a fact. One. I'll give it the front page and a headline with no dots in it.

correction_fail.speaker: editor
lines: A correction. Of what, exactly? That something was seen? It was seen.
I've run this paper since Truman. Come back when you've read a year of it instead of a day.
That was pushy. I'm allowed to say that. I'm the pushy one.

page.speaker: editor
lines: The letters started the next morning. Half the county. I kept every one. The file's in the morgue, third drawer, if you want it. Nobody's asked in years.
Letters to the editor are the county's diary, honey. Read them properly.

letters.speaker: editor
lines: Anyone write in who wasn't scared?
A university biologist. Says a sandhill crane, way off its migration. Tall as a man, grey, and a red patch on the head.
Red patch. Car headlights. That would do it.

passives.line: A biologist who writes to a weekly the same week, with a species, a height and a colour. Letters from scientists are never that tidy. Letters from somebody who wants a word printed are.

options.text: Could we see the letter file?
We're with the state. Open the December 1967 drawer.
We'll let you get the paper out.

morgue.speaker: editor
lines: The state. Took you twenty-seven years. Fine. December '67 is the bottom drawer, and it's mostly the bridge.
There's a woman in it who shouldn't be. From Sutton. Came in the week before it fell, asking what you're asking, with a man in a grey suit who never said a word.
I never ran her name. Her car turned up in Gallipolis and I never ran that either. I was told it wasn't a story.
Sutton. A woman from Sutton, in December 1967. That is the Office. That is Gus.

morgue_fail.speaker: editor
lines: The state. The state sent a woman last spring with a briefcase and a better lie than yours.
Get out of my morgue. The deputy will want to know who's impersonating Charleston in his town, and I'm going to tell him.
He's not wrong. I am the state. I'd rather he didn't find out from the deputy.
